page.overview:
Who is Ingold?

Ingold was a Man of Gondor and a soldier of the realm.

During the War of the Ring, he was the leader of the soldiers guarding Forannest, the northern gate of the Rammas Echor as it was being repaired just before the start of the Siege of Gondor. He permitted Gandalf and Pippin through the gate, having recognized the wizard immediately, but he enquired after Pippin's business in Minas Tirith as Gondorians of the time did not trust foreigners and Halflings were almost completely unknown to him, aside from the one mentioned in Boromir's dream.

Days after Gandalf had passed, an army out of Mordor crossed the river Anduin at Cair Andros and descended on Ingold's position. He retreated with those of his men who survived back to the city, reporting that the northern road had fallen into the hands of the enemy. This was woeful news in Minas Tirith, because it was thought to mean that the Rohirrim could not come to their aid (though in fact the Riders were able to find another route, the long-forgotten Stonewain Valley).

The name Ingold likely had close etymological ties with the word Ingoldo, meaning 'the Ñoldor' in Quenya.
